segments.t: Determined to sign iconic actor Fabrice Luchini, Andréa visits him at his Paris apartment. Luchini admits he has quit his rival agent Bréhier, but unexpectedly reveals that he plans to manage his own career without any agency. Listen to their conversation in French first.
C'est ouvert! Tu veux du thé?
Non merci, ça va.
Comment tu vas? Tu as l'air dans tous tes états.
Moi, je suis plutôt déprimé. J'ai raté un film de James Bond.
Alors j'ai quitté Bréhier.
C'est bien!
Ne t'emballe pas. Je vais faire une pause agent.
C'est-à-dire?
Je n'ai aucun film de prévu.
Je fais du théâtre, je n'ai besoin de personne.
Je suis désolé, je t'aimais vraiment bien, Andréa.
C'est comme se faire larguer alors qu'on n'a jamais été ensemble.
Oui, c'est un peu ça.
Je l'ai perdue pour toujours.
Et si on allait au théâtre ce soir, puis dîner?
Ça me plairait.
Let's explore how Andréa connects with Luchini on a deeply personal level.
C'est ouvert! Tu veux du thé?
'It's open! Would you like tea?' Fabrice welcomes Andréa into his chaotic apartment. This handy phrase literally translates as 'You want some tea?'. In French, this is perfectly fine.
Non merci, ça va.
'No thanks, I'm fine.' Andréa politely declines refreshment. You can say this whenever you want to casually say that things are okay. A standard way to speak in French.
Comment tu vas? Tu as l'air dans tous tes états.
'How are you? You seem in a state.' Fabrice notices her agitated expression. This idiom literally means 'in all your states'. In French, you will hear this.
Moi, je suis plutôt déprimé. J'ai raté un film de James Bond.
'Me, I'm pretty depressed. I missed out on a James Bond movie.' Fabrice shares his disappointment. In French, you'd use a structure that translates as 'I have missed'. The French say this often.
Alors j'ai quitté Bréhier.
'So I left Bréhier.' Fabrice drops the bombshell about firing his agent. It translates closer to 'So I have left'. In French, this is quite common.
C'est bien!
'That's good!' Andréa can barely contain her excitement. You'll hear this daily to express approval. This is how you say it in French.
Ne t'emballe pas. Je vais faire une pause agent.
'Don't get carried away. I am going to take an agent break.' Fabrice immediately dampens her hopes. In the negative, this handy chunk tells someone not to overreact. A handy phrase in French.
C'est-à-dire?
'Meaning?' Andréa asks him to clarify his strange decision. Literally 'that is to say', it is perfect for asking for details. A useful expression in French.
Je n'ai aucun film de prévu.
'I have no films planned.' Fabrice explains his schedule. This handy sentence means 'nothing planned'. This is very typical in French.
Je fais du théâtre, je n'ai besoin de personne.
'I'm doing theatre, I don't need anyone.' Fabrice boasts of his theatrical independence. It is built from the idea of 'having need of'. A common chunk in French.
Je suis désolé, je t'aimais vraiment bien, Andréa.
'I am sorry, I really liked you, Andréa.' Fabrice expresses genuine fondness for her. You'd use this to express affection for a person rather than romantic love. You will hear this in French.
C'est comme se faire larguer alors qu'on n'a jamais été ensemble.
'It's like getting dumped when you were never even together.' Andréa laments the strange situation. This expression literally means 'to make yourself dumped'. This is perfectly natural in French.
Oui, c'est un peu ça.
'Yes, that's kind of it.' Fabrice chuckles at her candid observation. It is a very natural way to agree mildly. In French, it works nicely.
Je l'ai perdue pour toujours.
'I lost her forever.' Andréa opens up about her heartbreak over Colette. Literally 'for always', this shows permanence. The French use this a lot.
Et si on allait au théâtre ce soir, puis dîner?
'What if we went to the theatre tonight, then had dinner?' Fabrice surprises her with a friendly invitation. This idiom is the standard way to suggest an activity. In French, it sounds perfect.
Ça me plairait.

'I would like that.' Andréa warmly accepts his offer for a night out. It translates literally as 'that would please me'. This is standard in French. Now let's listen to the full conversation between Andréa and Luchini once again.
C'est ouvert! Tu veux du thé?
Non merci, ça va.
Comment tu vas? Tu as l'air dans tous tes états.
Moi, je suis plutôt déprimé. J'ai raté un film de James Bond.
Alors j'ai quitté Bréhier.
C'est bien!
Ne t'emballe pas. Je vais faire une pause agent.
C'est-à-dire?
Je n'ai aucun film de prévu.
Je fais du théâtre, je n'ai besoin de personne.
Je suis désolé, je t'aimais vraiment bien, Andréa.
C'est comme se faire larguer alors qu'on n'a jamais été ensemble.
Oui, c'est un peu ça.
Je l'ai perdue pour toujours.
Et si on allait au théâtre ce soir, puis dîner?
Ça me plairait.
Although Luchini refuses to sign immediately, Andréa has built a genuine friendship with him. Remember the everyday idiom for getting carried away: s'emballer. See you next time!
À demain!
